newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Debt stalled ahead of Greenspan testimony.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Debt stalled ahead of Greenspan testimony.

text.p: Implied volatility of debt options on LIFFE edged up slightly in thin volumes on Wednesday as investors waited for Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan to begin his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony, brokers said.
Trade was slightly weighted to the put side, they said.

"The paper is generally mixed but if you can put a spin on it would be put buying for choice," said a trader at a French brokerage in London. "There's a little bit of nervousness in front of Humphrey-Hawkins."
The broker quoted June BTP 130.00 straddles at 7.30 percent, compared with 7.17 percent at the close on Tuesday.
Around 2,000 lots had been traded by around 1400 GMT, he said.
March BTP futures were quoted at 130.30 at 1416 GMT, down 24 basis points on Tuesday's pit settlement. June BTPs were down 0.27 at 129.70.
Greenspan gives testimony on the state of the U.S. economy to the Senate Banking Committee at 1500 GMT.
Analysts expect him to describe the economy in upbeat terms but also to include some words of caution about the course of inflation and perhaps the stock market.
Another broker at a British investment house said volatility of December Euromark puts was quoted at about 20 percent at the 96.25 strike and around 18.8 percent at the 96.25 straddle.
He said both were steady on Tuesday's close and had attracted total volume of around 3,000 lots.
December Euromarks were quoted at 96.57, down 0.02 at 1419 GMT.
